title: Any man who embraces the call may be ordained to preach
setting: Edward Partridge was a hatter from Painesville, Ohio, and a member of Sidney Rigdon’s congregation. His wife, Lydia, joined the Church after missionaries preached there in November 1830. Edward wanted to meet Joseph Smith first, so he came to New York with Rigdon and then asked for baptism. Joseph dictated this revelation for him on 9 December 1830 near Fayette. Joseph baptized him on 11 December, and Rigdon ordained him an elder on 15 December.
summary: The voice speaks as the Lord God and tells Edward that his sins are forgiven. Edward is called to preach as with the voice of a trumpet. Sidney Rigdon is to lay hands on him so he receives the Holy Ghost. Edward is to cry, “Hosanna, blessed be the name of the most high God”. Then the revelation widens its call to all men. Anyone who comes to Sidney Rigdon and Joseph Smith embracing this call may be ordained and sent out. It closes with the voice, as Jesus Christ, saying he will suddenly come to his temple.

contextNote.title: From one man’s call to every man’s
contextNote.text: The Church in late 1830 had few elders for a growing field. Verses 1–3 call one man, Edward Partridge, who had only just arrived. Verses 4–5 then extend “this calling and commandment” to all men who come forward. Verse 7 sets the one condition: they must embrace it “with singleness of heart”. Verse 8 gives the reason for haste, since the Lord says he will “suddenly come to my temple”. In this passage, singleness of heart means undivided commitment, and that is what qualifies a man to be sent.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 30–36 teaches that the Lord prepares people for the work he wants them to do. What does verse 2 say the Holy Ghost will teach Edward Partridge, and why would a brand-new preacher need that?
reviewNote: Read all 8 verses. Official heading gives 9 December 1830, near Fayette, to Edward Partridge. JSP introduction supplied Partridge’s background, Lydia’s conversion, and the baptism (11 December) and ordination (15 December) dates; JSP notes the 11 December baptism date may come from Joseph Smith’s history rather than independent memory. The 2025 CFM lesson does not cite section 36 by verse, so ldsText draws on its general preparation theme. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
